saints.name: St. Sebastian
saints.title: Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A soldier of Rome who secretly served Christ and encouraged the martyrs until he shed his own blood…
biography: Sebastian was a soldier of Rome, said by his ancient acts to have been born at Narbonne and bred at Milan, who entered the army about 283 and rose to be a captain of the praetorian guard under Diocletian, his faith unknown to the emperor. From that post he secretly strengthened the imprisoned Christians, among them the twin deacons Marcus and Marcellian, whose very parents he won for Christ.

Discovered about 286, he was condemned to be shot by the Mauritanian archers, who left him, says the Golden Legend, bristling with arrows like a hedgehog. Irene, the widow of the martyr Castulus, found him alive and nursed him; recovered, he waylaid Diocletian on a stairway and denounced his cruelty, and the emperor had him beaten to death with clubs and thrown into the great sewer.

He died about 288, and a matron named Lucina buried him in the catacombs on the Appian Way, where the basilica of San Sebastiano stands. Soldier, marksman's target, and pattern of endurance, he is patron of soldiers, archers, and athletes; in the Middle Ages he was among the most invoked against the plague, Rome having been freed by his intercession in 680.
saints.knownFor: His martyrdom by arrows under Diocletian.
